rationales.F01: Deafness and mutism are not directly related to the vulvar swelling.
rationales.F02: A slowly enlarging vulvar swelling could be indicative of several conditions, including Bartholin’s abscess or a vulvar cyst.
rationales.F03: The sudden increase in pain is more consistent with an abscess or other inflammatory condition.
rationales.F10: The initial clinical diagnosis of Bartholin’s abscess was based on the presentation of the swelling and signs of inflammation.
rationales.F11: The absence of signs of inflammation in the 5x5 cm swelling suggests it may not be an abscess.
rationales.F12: The firm, non-cystic nature of the mass and the intact hymen suggest that the swelling may not be related to a Bartholin’s abscess or other conditions that would involve the vaginal canal.
